hints: Separate Manhattan distance into x and y contributions.
After sorting one coordinate, each value's distance to all earlier values uses a prefix sum.
Add i*value minus the sum of earlier values for each sorted position i.
analogy: On a number line, the distance from a new rightmost point to earlier points is its coordinate repeated minus their coordinate sum.
example: For points (0,0),(2,0),(1,1), pair distances are 2,2,2, summing to 6.
algorithm: Sort all x coordinates and independently sort all y coordinates. For each sorted list, keep a prefix sum and add i*value-prefix to the answer at zero-based index i. Sum both coordinate contributions using a sufficiently wide integer.
correctness: Sorting ensures every earlier value is at most the current one, so i*value-prefix is exactly the sum of distances to earlier points. Every unordered pair is counted once on each axis.
complexity: For n points, O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
